frontMatter.introduction:
At Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), we are committed to delivering innovative, responsible, and technology-driven logistics solutions that meet the evolving needs of our global customers. Our end-to-end services—including international freight, warehousing, transport, and returns management—are underpinned by a strong focus on operational excellence, ethical practices, and environmental responsibility.

This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) Manual provides the operational foundation for maintaining consistency, compliance, and continuous improvement across all ASCG facilities. It supports our belief that transparency, accountability, and precision are essential to enabling a sustainable and efficient supply chain.
frontMatter.objective:
This SOP Manual has been developed to:

Standardize key logistics, warehousing, and administrative processes across all ASCG operations.
Ensure alignment with applicable national and international regulations (e.g., ISO 27001, HSE, GDPR).
Promote safety, efficiency, and environmental stewardship within supply chain activities.
Reinforce a workplace culture based on integrity, inclusivity, and innovation.
Empower employees, contractors, and partners to perform their roles with clarity and responsibility.
frontMatter.scope:
This SOP Manual applies to all ASCG employees, contractors, and third-party logistics partners involved in the planning, execution, and oversight of supply chain services. It covers operations at the following locations:

United Kingdom, UAE, Germany (site address table omitted).
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
To ensure the relevance, effectiveness, and legal alignment of all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) included in this Manual, the following review mechanism is implemented across ASCG:

1. Frequency of Review

All SOPs shall be reviewed annually by the assigned Policy Owner or Functional Lead.
Interim reviews may be triggered by:
Changes in regulatory or legal frameworks
Organisational restructuring or operational shifts
Significant ESG or compliance findings
Feedback or incidents from operational teams

2. Responsible Parties

Environmental SOPs: HSE Manager / Sustainability Lead
Labour & Human Rights SOPs: People Director / HR Manager
Ethics & Compliance SOPs: Compliance Officer / Legal Counsel
Procurement & Supplier SOPs: Procurement Director / ESG Lead
Information & Data Governance: IT Director / Compliance Officer

3. Review Process

Each SOP will be assessed for:
Relevance and accuracy of procedural content
Alignment with Reconomy Group's ESG strategy
Compliance with local and international regulations
All updates must be documented and submitted for Executive Leadership Team (ELT) endorsement before publication.

sops.title: Ensuring Safe, Ergonomic, and Mentally Healthy Working Conditions

blocks.text: Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, is committed to promoting safe, ergonomically sound, and psychologically supportive working environments. This SOP outlines the standards, controls, and proactive measures in place to minimise physical strain, reduce workplace injuries, and support employee mental wellbeing across all ASCG sites and functions, including hybrid, remote, and on-site roles.
To provide clear guidelines for:
This SOP applies to all permanent, temporary, contractual, and third-party employees working at or on behalf of ASCG globally. It encompasses:

rows.definition: The science of designing the workplace to fit the worker’s physical capabilities
Repetitive Strain Injury – musculoskeletal damage due to repetitive tasks
A workplace culture in which employees feel secure to express concerns, emotions, and ideas
Display Screen Equipment – includes desktops, laptops, and tablets

responsibilities: Oversee wellbeing and ergonomics policies across the business
Lead ergonomic assessments and compliance checks
Ensure team members receive relevant assessments and resources
Provide DSE-compliant equipment and workstation setup
Follow ergonomic guidelines and participate in wellbeing initiatives

steps.heading: 6.5 Physical Safety and Comfort at Work

body.text: Ergonomic or mental health concerns may be raised via:

sections.title: References
items: Mental Health Campaign Reports (“Wear It Green” Week)

blocks.text: At Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, we are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where every individual, regardless of background, feels valued and has equitable access to opportunities. This SOP outlines the actions, infrastructure, and behavioural practices embedded in our people strategy to continuously foster diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI).
To institutionalise workplace equality beyond legal compliance through proactive inclusion measures, accessibility improvements, inclusive communication, and unbiased facilities management.
This SOP applies to all permanent, temporary, contractual, and third-party workers across all ASCG locations globally.

rows.definition: Creating a culture that recognises and respects diverse backgrounds and experiences.
Ensuring fair treatment, access, and opportunity tailored to individual needs.
Designing spaces, systems, and processes usable by all, including people with disabilities.
Individuals who face systemic barriers due to gender identity, race, ethnicity, age, religion, disability, or sexual orientation.

responsibilities: Oversee program implementation and performance reporting
Deliver training, process feedback, and monitor compliance
Ensure infrastructure is inclusive and accessible
Comply with inclusive policies and report observed biases

substeps.text: Mandatory training on inclusive and bias-free language for all people managers (annually).
Internal documents and templates are to avoid gendered assumptions or exclusive terms.
Encouragement of pronoun use in internal systems and digital signatures (voluntary).
Gender-neutral washrooms implemented during all new facility builds and major renovations.
All restrooms and prayer/quiet rooms to include signage that reflects inclusivity.
Sites with more than 100 employees will have at least one multi-purpose wellness room.
All job advertisements use neutral language and list accommodations available during interviews.
Interview panel composition must include at least one trained DEI interviewer.
Pay equity audits are performed annually by role bands and regions.
Support for voluntary employee-led groups (e.g. Working Parents, Multicultural Network, Disability Inclusion Circle).
Internal DEI bulletin updated monthly featuring employee spotlights, events, and global inclusion days.

steps.heading: 6.5 Local Community and Supply Chain Inclusion

substeps.text: Site leadership encouraged to engage with VCSE (Voluntary, Community, and Social Enterprises) for local hiring.
Site-level inclusion projects (e.g. hosting job readiness workshops for underrepresented youth or differently-abled applicants).
Unconscious bias training for all supervisors and team leads.
Inclusion feedback is a standing topic in monthly one-on-one check-ins.

body.text: Employees can raise concerns or ideas through:

substeps.text: Directly to People Partners
ASCG Grievance Mechanism (confidential and non-retaliatory)

sops.title: Reduction of Energy Consumption of IT Infrastructure

blocks.text: Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, recognises the environmental impact of IT operations and is committed to reducing the energy consumption of its digital infrastructure. This SOP outlines technical and operational measures for improving energy efficiency across ASCG’s server rooms, data centres, user devices, and IT support facilities.

To minimise the carbon footprint and energy usage associated with IT infrastructure by integrating smart technologies, green procurement, and operational best practices in alignment with ASCG’s Environmental Roadmap and Reconomy’s low-carbon vision.
This SOP applies to all ASCG-controlled and -outsourced IT infrastructure, including but not limited to:

Data centres
On-site server rooms
Office-based IT equipment
Cloud services contracted under ASCG
IT procurement and maintenance activities

rows.definition: The use of software to simulate hardware functionality, allowing multiple virtual systems to run on a single physical system.
IT equipment that meets or exceeds ENERGY STAR or equivalent certifications.
A standard metric for measuring the energy efficiency of a data centre.
A layout strategy that separates hot and cold airflows in server rooms for efficient cooling.

responsibilities: Strategic oversight, target setting, and implementation of energy-efficient initiatives
Monitor energy usage, implement infrastructure-level upgrades, and report PUE monthly
Ensure all new IT equipment procured meets ASCG’s energy efficiency standards
Collaborate on HVAC upgrades and cooling optimisation
Practice energy-saving habits (e.g. switching off monitors, using power-saving modes)

body.text:
Replace outdated servers and desktops with ENERGY STAR-certified models by FY2030.
Standardise laptops with lower power consumption (max 45W TDP processors for general use).
Default all computers and monitors to auto-sleep after 10 minutes of inactivity.

Consolidate physical servers by 10% using virtualisation platforms (e.g. VMware, Hyper-V) by FY2028.
Shift 40% of eligible on-prem workloads to cloud providers offering carbon-neutral services (e.g. Azure, AWS Green).

Install cold aisle containment solutions in all server rooms with more than 10 racks.
Raise server room temperature setpoints to 24°C ±1°C where thermally safe.
Upgrade to variable-speed fans and liquid-based cooling systems where feasible.

Deploy smart meters and environment sensors to monitor IT energy consumption.
Track and report Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) at quarterly intervals.
Conduct annual energy audits for all major ASCG server locations.

Conduct annual training for IT and facilities teams on energy reduction practices.
Promote “Power Down” campaigns encouraging employees to shut down unused systems.
Use digital dashboards to visualise energy savings from IT changes.

blocks.text:
IT and Facilities teams to submit annually Energy Consumption Reports to the ESG Compliance Team.
Employees may submit feedback or suggestions for further improvements via:
a) Internal Helpdesk Portal

sops.title: Reduction of Material Consumption through Process Optimization

blocks.text: Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, is committed to optimising operations in ways that minimise material waste, support sustainability, and drive cost-effective practices. This SOP outlines structured actions, supported by technology and process enhancements, that enable ASCG to reduce its material consumption across key operations.

To ensure that all sites within ASCG implement measures that limit excessive use of materials—particularly packaging, chemicals, cleaners, and energy-intensive parts—through cleaner technologies, reuse/reconditioning, predictive maintenance, and operational discipline.
This SOP applies to all ASCG operational and warehouse sites globally, including third-party vendors or partners that use ASCG’s infrastructure for material handling, maintenance, or processing.

rows.definition: Systematic methods used to increase efficiency and reduce input wastage.
Components that have been restored to usable condition through minor repairs.
Scheduled servicing to reduce breakdowns and extend equipment life.
A system using shredding equipment to repurpose waste cardboard into padding.
A method of cleaning using ultrasound and water-based solutions to reduce chemicals.

responsibilities: Implement material-saving tools (e.g., shredders, cleaning stations)
Ensure re-use of materials wherever possible and enforce maintenance SOPs
Monitor day-to-day use of packaging, chemicals, and ensure compliance
Track data related to waste reduction, chemical use, and performance reporting
Comply with optimisation procedures and report material inefficiencies

substeps.text: Install cardboard shredders at each main warehouse.
Feed approved used cartons into shredders to convert into protective padding.
Operators must inspect for metal/screws in folded boxes prior to shredding.
Ensure cutting rollers are oiled periodically, and machine performance is logged weekly.
Implement ultrasonic or water-based washing for parts instead of solvent-based cleaning.
Use de-ionised water during battery topping
Avoid overfilling batteries—monitor ambient temperatures to reduce unnecessary top-ups.
Introduce automated low-flow sprayers and chemical dispensers to control usage.
Weekly checklists to inspect wear/tear on packaging stations and conveyor belts.
Use reconditioned parts (gears, switches, filters) during equipment servicing where safe.
Maintain logs of reused vs. new parts at site level.
Train staff on material-conscious behaviour: e.g., reusing packaging void fill, limiting tape usage.
Display process charts near machinery for reminders on material conservation protocols.
Monthly toolbox talks on material-saving hacks at the operator level.

sops.title: Internal Sorting and Disposal of Waste According to Waste Streams

blocks.text: At Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, responsible waste management is an essential part of our environmental sustainability and compliance strategy. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) outlines the actions, roles, and standards that ensure all operational waste is properly sorted according to defined waste streams and disposed of through responsible methods such as reuse, recycling, or recovery.

To establish consistent procedures across all ASCG sites for segregating, handling, storing, and disposing of waste in line with UK & Germany waste legislation, Simpler Recycling rules, and our internal 2025 Waste Management Mapping and Inventory Plan.
This SOP applies to all ASCG operational and warehouse sites worldwide, encompassing employees, site managers, cleaners, material handlers, contractors, and third-party logistics providers.

rows.definition: A defined category of waste such as wood, electronic waste, metal, food, paper, or plastic.
Dry Mixed Recycling: includes card, paper, plastics, cans, etc.
Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment.
UK government regulation effective 31st March 2025, mandating standardized recycling and bin categories.
Improper disposal (e.g., food in plastics) that makes waste unrecyclable or violates provider rules.

responsibilities: Ensure bins are available, labelled, and matched to correct waste streams. Track compliance.
Follow signage, training, and dispose of waste correctly. Report issues.
Comply with ASCG waste sorting standards while on-site.
Monitor audit results, report waste KPIs, and ensure legal alignment.
Maintain cleanliness around disposal stations and signage upkeep.

body.text: Waste must be sorted into the following streams:

General Waste
Dry Mixed Recycling (DMR)
Wood Waste
Food Waste
Cardboard & Paper
Plastic Packaging
WEEE Waste
Scrap Metal
Sanitary Waste
Each bin will be colour-coded and labelled using multilingual signage.

At Rest Areas: General waste, plastic, food, and coffee waste.
Admin/Office Areas: Paper, card, glass bottles, tins/cans.
Operations Floor: Wood, plastics, general waste, recycling.
External Areas: Large-scale wood, WEEE, scrap metal containers.
Waste Stream Sorting Table
rows: Clean plastics, cans, dry paper, card

body.text:
Waste Disposal Path

Employee Generates Waste
↓
Reads Bin Label Signage
↓
Sorts Waste into Correct Bin
↓
Bin Collected by Facilities
↓
Weight/Volume Tracked
↓
Vendor Pickup for Reuse/Recycling/Landfill

Simpler Recycling training mandatory for all staff (delivered quarterly).
Posters and visuals placed at all disposal points in all major languages.
Waste sorting refreshers included in induction and toolbox talks.

Each site records bin pickups (in tonnes or number of collections).
Weekly waste inspections by facilities team and data logged.
Non-compliance (e.g., DMR contamination) must be logged and corrected.

Special signage and briefings developed for HGV drivers and external workers.
Site induction programs now include short waste compliance brief.

narrative.text:
Site audits (e.g. Hunters Point, April 2025) will validate compliance.
Monthly data collected in the Waste Management Mapping system.

blocks.text: Waste vendor rejections due to contamination (e.g., liquids in DMR) will trigger a root cause analysis.
Remediation actions may include:

Re-training of staff
Contractor re-briefings
Physical re-layout of bins
Feedback loops from Waste Solutions Providers

sops.title: ESG Due Diligence Program on Third Parties

blocks.text: Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, recognises that responsible third-party engagement is essential to maintaining ethical, sustainable, and low-impact supply chains. This SOP outlines ASCG’s ESG due diligence framework for assessing the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices of our suppliers and third-party business partners.

To implement a structured ESG due diligence process that ensures third-party partners meet ASCG’s ethical, environmental, labour, and compliance expectations, while also reducing ESG-related risks in our supply chain.
This SOP applies to all ASCG departments engaging third-party services—including Procurement, Compliance, Legal, and Operations—across all operational regions.

rows.definition: Any external organisation or individual providing goods or services to ASCG (e.g. suppliers, vendors, contractors, agents).
A systematic review of a third party’s ESG performance prior to onboarding or contract renewal.
A framework that applies enhanced scrutiny to third parties classified as high-risk.
An on-site or remote evaluation of a third party’s environmental practices, labour conditions, and ethical standards.

responsibilities: Oversee implementation, risk mapping, and audit findings
Trigger ESG due diligence during vendor selection or contract renewal
Support in supplier coordination and improvement tracking
Provide documentation and participate in audits and continuous improvement
Monitor alignment across the group and assist in benchmarking efforts

body.text: Categorise third parties as Low / Medium / High risk based on:

Geographic operation (e.g. high-risk countries)
Type of product/service
Past compliance records
Labour-intensive or environmentally intensive processes
All third parties must submit a completed ASCG ESG Self-Assessment Questionnaire covering:

Environmental compliance (e.g. emissions, waste, packaging)
Labour rights (e.g. child labour, working hours, freedom of association)
Governance indicators (e.g. bribery, corruption, transparency)
Supporting documents required include:

Supplier Code of Conduct (signed)
Environmental policies or certifications (ISO 14001, etc.)
Modern Slavery or Human Rights policies
High-risk third parties will undergo a full on-site ESG audit at least once every year.
Audit checklist includes:

Waste disposal and material handling
Labour practices and workplace safety
Discrimination and grievance mechanisms
Responsible sourcing and traceability

ESG audit findings are scored and benchmarked across suppliers.
Annual improvement plans are requested from suppliers scoring below threshold.
Risk rating is updated based on progress, audit results, or any adverse events.

narrative.text:
Non-compliance triggers a Corrective Action Plan (CAP) with deadlines tracked by Procurement and ESG Compliance.
Repeat or severe breaches may result in suspension or deactivation of the supplier relationship.
Follow-up audits are conducted to verify closure of high-priority findings.

All records (questionnaires, audit reports, risk ratings) are maintained in ASCG’s Third-Party ESG Tracker.
ESG performance data is reviewed annually and summarised in ASCG’s internal ESG performance report.
Any severe issues are escalated to the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and Reconomy Group ESG Committee.

sops.title: Implementation of a Records Retention Schedule for Third-Party Data

blocks.text: Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, acknowledges its responsibility to handle third-party data in a secure, efficient, and compliant manner. This SOP outlines the structured process for implementing a records retention schedule to ensure that all data associated with suppliers, contractors, vendors, and other third-party entities is retained only for the period necessary to meet business, legal, and regulatory obligations.
To establish a formal, documented schedule for the retention and disposal of third-party data across all departments, ensuring:

Legal and regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR, UK Data Protection Act)
Operational efficiency through reduced data clutter
Protection of sensitive business and third-party information
Support for audits, litigation, and internal reviews

This SOP applies to all third-party data managed across ASCG operations, including digital and physical records, whether generated internally or provided by the third party.
Applicable across Procurement, Legal, Compliance, IT, Finance, and ESG departments globally.

rows.definition: Information received from or related to external partners such as suppliers, vendors, logistics providers, contractors, etc.
A schedule specifying how long various categories of third-party data must be retained.
Secure and approved destruction or deletion of records at the end of the retention period.
A temporary override of the retention period due to anticipated or actual litigation or regulatory investigation.

responsibilities: Oversight of compliance with retention periods and data protection regulations
Maintenance and periodic update of the records retention schedule
Implementation of system-based data retention and secure deletion protocols
Classification of data types and adherence to the retention schedule
Awareness and execution of appropriate data retention and disposal protocols

body.text: Each department must classify the third-party data it handles into clear categories, for example:

Contracts and Agreements
Vendor Onboarding Documents
ESG Audit Reports
Payment and Invoice Records
Insurance Certificates
Licenses and Certifications
Communication Records
Grievance and Compliance Logs
The Data Retention Schedule must include the retention period for each category based on:

Legal or regulatory requirements (e.g., HMRC: 6 years for financial records)
Contractual obligations with third parties
Business value and operational need

IT must configure automated deletion settings where feasible (e.g., emails, vendor portals, ERP).
Manual checks and semi-annual audits will be conducted for physical and non-integrated systems.
If litigation, audit, or regulatory matters require extension:

Data will be flagged as “on hold”
Retention override must be approved by Legal or Compliance
Disposition resumes only upon formal release of hold

Every deletion or archive must be logged.
Proof of compliance must be stored for audit purposes (date of deletion, responsible person/system, reason for deletion).
IT to maintain retention compliance logs available to internal auditors.

narrative.text:
Retention schedule reviewed annually by the Compliance Team.
Legal, operational, and technological changes trigger ad hoc updates.
Non-compliance to be addressed via internal audit escalation protocols.

blocks.text:
All relevant staff to receive annual data retention training.
Retention schedules to be embedded in ERP/procurement/finance systems.
Regular reminders shared on ASCG’s intranet and during quarterly compliance reviews.

sops.title: Energy Reduction Across ASCG Facilities and Operations

blocks.text:
Advanced Supply Chain Group Limited (ASCG), a Reconomy Group company, recognises energy consumption as one of the key contributors to its operational carbon footprint. With a commitment to environmental stewardship, this SOP establishes a structured approach to reducing energy use across our infrastructure—spanning logistics centres, warehouses, IT, HVAC systems, lighting, and general office consumption.

This SOP supports compliance with the ISO 14001:2015 Environmental Management System and contributes to ASCG’s Net-Zero and Circular Economy objectives.

To implement energy-efficient practices and technologies across all ASCG sites by reducing reliance on non-renewable energy, improving system efficiency, and encouraging employee behaviour that contributes to energy savings.
This SOP applies to all ASCG facilities and covers energy consumption associated with:

IT infrastructure (servers, data centres)
HVAC systems
Lighting systems
Warehouse and logistics operations
Office utilities and appliances

rows.definition: Achieving the same or improved output using less energy.
Light-emitting diodes that use up to 80% less energy than traditional bulbs.
Systems that monitor and report real-time energy use for optimisation.
Technology used to control lighting, HVAC, and other facility systems automatically.

responsibilities: Implement and maintain energy-saving infrastructure upgrades
Source energy-efficient equipment and certified suppliers
Report performance against energy KPIs and Net-Zero roadmap
Oversee energy optimisation in data centres and IT equipment
Follow energy protocols and report inefficiencies

body.text:
Conduct annual energy audits for each ASCG site.
Benchmark electricity, gas, and diesel usage per sq. metre and per unit of output.
Identify and prioritise high-consumption assets (servers, chillers, compressors, conveyors).

Replace outdated lighting with 100% LED systems by 2030.
Install motion sensors in low-traffic warehouse aisles and meeting rooms.
Implement variable speed drives (VSDs) on motors, conveyors, HVAC fans.
Replace gas heating with air source heat pumps where feasible.
Introduce energy-efficient server racks with high-efficiency cooling.

Use virtualisation and cloud-based services to reduce on-site server loads.
Implement automatic sleep mode on unused desktop systems.
Adopt energy-efficient hardware for all office and warehouse PCs, printers, and networking gear.
Centralise printing with energy-star rated multi-function devices.

Install Building Management System (BMS) systems to manage lighting, HVAC and refrigeration.
Use smart thermostats with scheduling to avoid overnight HVAC usage.
Incorporate energy dashboards for real-time visibility.

Monthly awareness campaigns on energy conservation behaviour.
Set office thermostat guidelines (e.g., 21°C cooling, 19°C heating).
Encourage natural daylight use before switching on artificial lighting.
Promote “power-down protocol” at shift end for all non-critical systems.

narrative.text:
ESG team to compile monthly energy reports for leadership.
Quarterly review meetings to assess progress against Net-Zero Roadmap.
Performance outcomes to be published in ASCG’s Annual ESG Impact Report.

sections.title: References
items: Energy Technology List (ETL) for Procurement Standards

blocks.text:
Annual employee training on energy efficiency practices (mandatory).
Onboarding modules include “Energy-Conscious Operations”.
Site noticeboards and intranet portals to display monthly energy usage trends and achievements.
